title: 14-Inch MacBook Pro With M6 – Price, Specifications
metaDescription: Apple's 14-inch MacBook Pro with M6 starts at $1,999 and ships November 6. Specs, battery, ports, pre-order details and what Apple has not said yet.
excerpt: Apple announced the M6 14-inch MacBook Pro on October 27. Here is what changed, what did not, and what to check before you order.
answer: The new 14-Inch MacBook Pro with an M6 chip was announced by Apple on the 27th of October 2026. It starts from $1,999 and will be available to pre-order on the 28th October and ship on the 6th November. It has received some major upgrades with a 12-Core CPU, 12-Core GPU and up to 24 hours of battery, but Apple has not given us full details of the storage costs.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.body:
The new 14-Inch MacBook Pro with an M6 chip was announced in a press release on the 27th of October 2026. It starts from $1,999 in the United States, or $1,899 with education pricing. You’ll be able to pre-order from the 28th October at 10.10am PT. It will be available in stores and to customers on the 6th November.

The key upgrades to this MacBook are the new M6 chip with a 12-Core CPU and 12-Core GPU (2 extra each). It also has a faster Neural Engine. Apple has stated that it has up to 24 hours of battery life, the longest they’ve ever claimed.

Otherwise, there aren’t too many changes. This is a specification upgrade to the base model. The display, ports and colours are the same as previous models. If you have an M5 model it’s not a huge incentive to upgrade. However, if you have an Intel laptop you’ll have a much better reason.

Below we’ve outlined exactly what Apple have said, what third-party sources have said and what isn’t clear. We haven’t had any hands-on with these laptops.

sections.heading: Upgrades with the M6 Chip
sections.body:
Apple has stated that it has a 12-Core CPU (2 extra) and a 12-Core GPU (2 extra). Each core of the GPU also has a Neural Accelerator. It also has a 3rd Gen Ray Tracing engine and Dynamic Caching.

For Graphics Apple has stated it has up to 30% faster performance. This is when compared to the M5 chip, 10-Core CPU and 10-Core GPU. This will depend on the workload you’re doing and as always this is Apple’s claimed performance.

For AI, Apple has stated that it has a Dual 16-Core Neural Engine. This is up to 1.9x faster than the M5. It also has up to 25% faster on-device AI performance such as prompt processing for large language models. If you’re not running local models or using AI features much you might not even notice.

Apple has stated it has the fastest CPU core in the world. However, the press release doesn’t state what it’s faster than. This is marketing until reviews come out.

It has up to 170GB/s of memory bandwidth. However, MacRumors has stated in their latest headlines that this isn’t available on the base 16GB model. We weren’t able to see the details of this. If this is important to you then check Apple’s tech specs page for your configuration.

sections.heading: Memory & Storage
sections.body:
It has 16GB of unified memory as standard. This can be upgraded to 32GB. MacRumors has stated that it has 1TB of storage as standard and can be upgraded to 4TB.

MacRumors has also stated that the previous M5 model had a 512GB base model but this was removed in March. So this is partly due to what happened earlier this year.

If you’re most people you’ll be wondering if 16GB is enough. For everyday tasks like browsing, office, photo editing and light video editing it usually is. However, if you’re doing large video projects, large code builds, VMs or local AI models then having 32GB will give you more space. Unlike on a PC, you won’t be able to upgrade your memory as it’s built into the chip.

Storage is the same. You won’t be able to upgrade the internal drive like some Windows laptops. So make sure you know how much you’ll need and consider getting a fast external drive for storing archives.

sections.heading: Display, Design & Colours
sections.body:
It has a Liquid Retina XDR display with up to 1600 nits of HDR brightness and a 1,000,000:1 contrast ratio. The nano-texture option will help reduce reflections and glare if you’re working near windows or bright lights.

The press release doesn’t state if it’s an OLED or touch display. Based on the information from Apple it should not be. However, Apple did also announce an OLED Touchscreen MacBook Pro this week. MacRumors has stated that this model has an M5 Pro or M5 Max chip and is a completely different product.

It has two colours. Space Black and Silver. It also has an enclosure made from 100% recycled aluminium. The Space Black colour has an anodized seal to reduce fingerprints. The size and weight wasn’t mentioned.

It has a 12MP Centre Stage camera, Studio quality 3-Microphone array and 6-Speaker audio system with Spatial Audio.

sections.heading: Battery & Charging
sections.body:
Apple has stated it has up to 24 hours of battery life. This is the longest they’ve ever claimed. It also states that you’ll get the same performance whether you’re on battery or plugged in. This will depend on how you’re using it and what you have. Usually this amount of time will come from a light video playback test.

It has up to 14 hours extra for those upgrading from Intel-based models. Up to 4 hours extra if you’re upgrading from the M1.

With fast charging you’ll be able to charge it to 50% in around 30 minutes using a compatible high wattage USB-C adapter such as the 96W Power Adapter.

If you’re using your laptop for travel days this could be very useful.

sections.heading: Ports
sections.body:
Apple has included some great ports. It has an HDMI port, MagSafe 3, 3 Thunderbolt 4 ports, SDXC card slot and Headphone Jack.

It also has Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth 6. It can also support up to 2 external displays.

This means photographers can insert cards without using a dongle and presentors can plug straight in. The 3 Thunderbolt 4 ports will allow you to use docks, fast external drives and displays.

sections.heading: Software & Siri
sections.body:
It will come with macOS 27 (Golden Gate). It has Siri AI in Beta in macOS 27.2. It supports English, French, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese & Spanish.

Some features rely on models on the server and have daily limits. They will be a fee to get more access in the future. However, the amount isn’t mentioned in the press release.

macOS 27 will be installed on the laptop when you purchase. The Siri AI will only be available on macOS 27.2 and will be in Beta. This means you should expect a great experience using it as a normal Mac. However, the newest AI features will be constantly changing as they test them.

It has support for 6 languages. English, French, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese & Spanish. If you don’t use another language much then make sure it supports what you need.

This is a good reason to read the small print. If you’re buying this laptop for the new AI features then know that it is in Beta. We don’t know what the long term terms will be.

sections.heading: Should M5 owners upgrade?
sections.body:
Based on what Apple have said it has 2 extra CPU Cores, 2 extra GPU Cores, a faster Neural Engine and 24 hours of battery. This is a good upgrade between generations but not a massive one.

MacRumors has stated that it’s a specification upgrade over the M5. It also has a comment from a reader stating it has been $2,000 since a price increase in June. This means it’s effectively the same price. We weren’t able to confirm this.

If you recently bought an M5 then honestly, probably not. They’ve focused on the faster graphics and AI performance. A modest M5 will do almost everything you’ll need.

If you’re still on an M1 you’ll get up to 4 extra hours of battery. There will be a huge improvement with graphics and AI. If you’re on an intel laptop then you should notice a big difference.

sections.heading: Other Announcements
sections.body:
The 14-Inch MacBook Pro wasn’t the only announcement. MacRumors has a roundup of all the announcements. These include the M6 iMac, 8.5-Inch OLED iPad Mini with A20 Pro chip, S10 chip HomePod mini 2 and the OLED Touchscreen MacBook Pro mentioned above.

The iPad Mini starts from $699 after a second price increase this year. It has an IP67 rating but doesn’t have ProMotion. The HomePod mini 2 has a release date of October 30. The iPad Mini & iMac can be pre-ordered on the 28th October and released on the 6th November.

We’re using MacRumors for this. It’s a roundup page and not all products have prices.

Overall Apple have done a lot of refreshing. If you’re deciding between the M6 14-Inch & OLED model then make sure to compare the specs and prices on Apple’s site. They’re targeted at different budgets.

sections.heading: Who Should Buy?
sections.body:
If you’re upgrading from an Intel Mac or M1 then this is a great long lasting laptop with a great display and proper ports. Whilst it’s not cheap at $1,999 you’ll notice the improvements with battery life and performance.

Consider waiting if you want an OLED Touchscreen, more details on the price of your configuration or want to read some independent reviews. The claims from Apple are always the best case scenario and they’ll be testing them within days of the 6th November release.

If you recently bought an M5 MacBook Pro and are happy with it then skip this. You won’t really notice any improvements.

If you’re purchasing online make sure to check the returns policy. The education price is a great saving. $100 difference between $1,999 vs $1,899.

sections.heading: Checklist
sections.body:
Configuration

The real price of this laptop will depend on your configuration. The $1,999 price from Apple is for the base model. MacRumors has stated that this has 16GB of memory and 1TB of storage. Use the configurator to find out what your exact memory and storage will cost. If you’re keeping this laptop for years then consider adding AppleCare. Apple offer AppleCare+, AppleCare One and AppleCare One Family in the US.

Display Finish

It has an option for a nano-texture display. This will reduce reflections and glare. If you often work near windows, outside or with bright lights this is a great option. If you mostly work in a controlled environment then the standard glass may be sufficient. Check the configurator to see how much of a difference it makes. We couldn’t see this in the press release.

Memory Bandwidth

It has up to 170GB/s of memory bandwidth. MacRumors has a headline stating this isn’t available on the base 16GB model. We couldn’t see any details. Check the tech specs for your exact configuration. If you’re doing intensive graphics, video or local AI work then it’s worth checking.

Ports

It has a HDMI port, MagSafe 3, 3 Thunderbolt 4 ports and an SDXC card slot. Many people won’t need a dock. If you want fast charging then Apple has stated you can charge it to 50% in around 30 minutes using a compatible high wattage USB-C adapter such as the 96W Power Adapter. Make sure this is included in your configuration.

Trade In & Finance

You can get Apple Trade In credit to reduce the upfront cost. In the US you can get 0% APR Apple Card Monthly Installments. You can also get the Apple Upgrade lease from $38.99 per month for 36 months. This is leased from Klarna and is subject to approval. If you like changing your laptop often then this could be a good option. However, make sure to calculate how much it will cost you over 36 months.

Timing

Pre-orders started on the 28th October and it will ship on the 6th November. Apple usually have independent reviews within days. The return period will give you time to test the battery, fan noise and display. If you can wait a week or two then you’ll know a lot more than what Apple have claimed.

If you’re still unsure write down the 3 things you do most on your laptop. If none of these are affected by your current laptop then you may get the best price.

sections.heading: Overall
sections.body:
This is a sensible upgrade. It has 2 extra cores in the CPU and GPU, 24 hours of battery and the ports are the same. If you have an older laptop then this is a solid upgrade.

However, there are some things to be aware of. We haven’t seen the full price of the configurations. There is a note about the memory bandwidth on the base model and the AI features are in Beta with a future fee.

If you can then wait for independent battery and performance tests. Otherwise order with the return period in mind. This is just our opinion.

faq.q: How much is the 14-Inch MacBook Pro with M6?
faq.a: It starts from $1,999 in the US, or $1,899 with education pricing. Higher memory and storage options weren’t mentioned.

faq.q: When can I buy the M6 MacBook Pro?
faq.a: Pre-orders started on the 28th October at 10.10am PT. It will be shipped and in store on the 6th November 2026.
It has a 12-Core CPU, 12-Core GPU, Dual 16-Core Neural Engine, 16GB of memory (upgradable to 32), Liquid Retina XDR Display with up to 1600 nits of HDR brightness and up to 24 hours of battery.

faq.q: Is it an OLED or touchscreen?
faq.a: The 14-Inch M6 isn’t mentioned in the press release as being OLED or touchscreen. MacRumors has stated that Apple have also announced an OLED Touchscreen MacBook Pro with M5 Pro or M5 Max chip.

faq.q: Does it have an HDMI port and SD card slot?
faq.a: Yes. It has an HDMI port, MagSafe 3, 3 Thunderbolt 4 ports, SDXC card slot and headphone jack.

faq.q: Should I upgrade from an M5 MacBook Pro?
faq.a: Probably not. It has 2 extra CPU cores, 2 extra GPU cores and a faster Neural Engine. However, this will only really benefit those upgrading from an M1 or Intel laptop.
